question: An agent sells a turbo cooker with a marked price of ₹6,370 at a discount of 50%. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the turbo cooker?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A discount of 50% means the selling price is exactly half of the marked price.

SP = MP ÷ 2

SP = 6370 ÷ 2

SP = 3185

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,185.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 MP = ₹6,370

 
• 
 − 50% Discount

 
 SP = ?

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹6,370

Discount = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Amount

Discount Amount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × MP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = (50 ÷ 100) × 6370

⇒ Discount Amount = 1/2 × 6370

⇒ Discount Amount = 3185

⇒ SP = 6370 − 3185

⇒ SP = 3185

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,185.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), whereas Profit and Loss are calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are offered, the effective discount percentage is given by: [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100]%.

Selling Price Relation

SP can be expressed relative to both MP and CP: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.
